changedBeliefs: After exp 195/198/203/205 tightened `write_json_to_buf`'s per-cell body, exp 223 tested whether the remaining row-boundary control flow (per-iteration `if (row_index > 0)`, split `[` + `{` writes, empty-result path through the row loop) was still material. Peeling row 0 out of the loop fuses `[{` into a single 2-byte prelude, short-circuits empty results to `[]`, and drops the per-row branch from the shared body.

The per-row branch predicts well and the bracket fuse is byte-count noise on typical row shapes. Two order-flipped passes of `select_bytes_repeated_calls.dart` reproduce candidate-faster only at ~1-2% on 10-100 rows (inside the ~3% effect floor); the 1000-row lane collapses from -1.5% to -0.2% (drift), and the 1 row × 8 int cols lane trends candidate-slower on both passes (+0.4%, +4.6%). The `select_bytes_wide_cols.dart` single pass shows the same magnitude class with the load-bearing 10k × 8 int lane at +5.7% - a drift signature, not a real regression.

The 60-line encoder-body macro that lets row 0 and rows 1+ share one authoritative cell encoder is a maintenance cost every future encoder change has to reason about. A reproduced 1-2% win inside the harness noise floor does not justify carrying that macro on the hot path.
nextSignals: Do not retry per-row control-flow shaves in `write_json_to_buf` (branch peeling, prelude fusing, empty-result short-circuits) without a per-cell body that has shrunk enough to make the row-boundary work a larger relative share. The current baseline already spends most per-row wall inside the token memcpy + type-switched value write - shave that first.

The next `result-transfer-shape` implementation should target a larger mechanism: a per-cell SIMD path (aarch64 NEON escape scan or base64 encode over the existing scalar SWAR ceilings exp 201/216/218 charted), an algorithm change, or a transport-format change. Row-boundary micro-optimizations are settled below the focused-harness floor.

Keep `select_bytes_repeated_calls.dart` and `select_bytes_wide_cols.dart` as the durable gates for encoder-body work. The 1-row shapes on `repeated_calls.dart` remain SendPort-dominated at µs scale and cannot cleanly attribute per-query setup wins; use 10-100 row shapes for signal and treat 1-row lanes as regression guards rather than acceptance drivers.

The runtime prototype is preserved at `archive/exp-223`; a future encoder change that shrinks the per-cell body materially can cherry-pick the row peel to test whether row-boundary control flow re-enters the signal window.
